title: STILL PRESENT (r3): wrong-person awaiting UPDATE still executes the unguarded update_reference_call_status — the taken_over_at backstop is dead code and the race pin is vacuous
evidence: case sql.update_reference_call_status(config.db, id_uuid, sql.AwaitingCorrection, "", "contact_invalid", sql.ContactInitiated) ... WHERE id = $1 AND status = $5::reference_call_status (no taken_over_at clause) — and grep of server/src shows mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person is defined in sql.gleam:1891 but called NOWHERE
detail: apply_wrong_person's False arm still runs the status-only UPDATE; a take-over landing between the token read and the UPDATE matches (status stays contact_initiated) and dead-ends the row. The dedicated guarded SQL is never wired; the pin test (actions_integration_test:1729) calls the guarded SQL directly — vacuous by the round-4 definition.
recommended_fix: Wire the executed path: call sql.mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person(config.db, id_uuid) in apply_wrong_person's awaiting arm; add a POST-route race test that goes red when the backstop is neutralized.

title: STILL PRESENT (r3): co-nudge kind-tag exclusion is forward-only — legacy untagged co-nudge entries still match the delivery-failure find
evidence: WHERE e->>'detail' = $3 AND e->>'outcome' = 'delivered' AND NOT (e ? 'kind') — the kind tag was added only at df0ea22 (sweep.gleam co_nudge_entry); at 111e221 co-nudges were logged via outcomes_to_json with no kind, and attempts is append-only
detail: A bounce of the applicant's co-nudge address whose send_ref matches a pre-df0ea22 untagged entry still finds the referee row: pre-correction it fabricates awaiting_correction, post-correction (entry at >= corrected_at) it exhausts with referee_contact_invalid. The pin test only covers a kind-tagged entry.
recommended_fix: Exclude co-nudge sends structurally (match detail against the applicant's own send ids) or backfill/migrate existing attempts logs so legacy entries carry the exclusion marker.

title: STILL PRESENT (r3): Escape-to-close keydown handler remains on the menu div, a sibling of the focused ⋯ button — click-then-Escape still does nothing
evidence: html.div([...event.on("keydown", menu_escape_decoder(...))...], actions...) — the ⋯ button (line ~721) carries only event.on_click; after clicking it, focus stays on the button and keydown never bubbles to the sibling menu div
detail: The natural click-⋯-then-Escape flow cannot reach the handler; only keyboard users who tab INTO a menu item trigger it via bubbling. Menu div is not focusable (no tabindex/autofocus).
recommended_fix: Move the keydown handler onto the ⋯ button (or autofocus the menu on open) so the Escape key is reachable from the click-created focus point.
